label: The type mapping is organised per source language in eleven tables and the bridge is a separate orthogonal decision; sk-code has one Rust/TypeScript interop model and no source-language axis at all

serde_json::Value is the universal fallback for anything structured, unknown or a union of different types; it appears zero times in the sk-code Rust references and checklist, whose boundary list is closed with no escape hatch

refused is a first-class outcome with a printed reason and the function stays in its source language, with reasons phrased as design questions; sk-code has no do-not-port-this outcome so an agent facing an inexpressible type improvises
The type document is executable: tests/types_doc.rs includes it with include_str! and checks every row against the mapping so a row cannot drift from the code; types_doc appears zero times in sk-code

The C ABI keeps width and sign through std::ffi::c_* with long noted as 32 bits on Windows, size_t to usize and ssize_t/ptrdiff_t/intptr_t to isize; c_int, c_long, size_t, repr(C), extern C and the phrase C ABI each appear zero times in sk-code

C pointer mapping is decided by the neighbouring parameter, const char* to Option<&[u8]>, const byte pointer plus length to &[u8] with the length dropped, writable byte pointer to &mut [u8], written scalar pointer to Option<&mut T>, char** into a string to Option<&mut Option<usize>>, and the refusals name the design question; Option<&mut appears zero times in sk-code
char is refused in Java, Kotlin and C# for one stated reason, it is a UTF-16 code unit; this is the type-level twin of the UTF-16 ordering trap and sk-code has no UTF-16 rule anywhere

Unordered collections are refused while ordered ones cross as a Vec in their own order with repeated elements a mismatch; sk-code states the same principle as an obligation but not as the type-level consequence that an unordered collection must not cross
A map with non-string keys is refused because JSON object keys are strings, in Go, Java and C# with the identical note; sk-code has no rule about map key types at a boundary

Precision refusals are stated as arithmetic facts, decimal because a 128-bit decimal no JSON number keeps exactly and ulong/nint/nuint because they are wider than a JSON-safe integer; sk-code diagnoses the same problem but answers it with a versioned String, so the two contradict in method and agree in diagnosis

Go []byte becomes Vec<i64> a list of numbers not bytes, and a trailing error result is dropped rather than mapped while two or more other results cross as one serde_json::Value array; sk-code has no Go mapping

Python int becomes i64 not f64, bytes/bytearray/memoryview become Vec<u8>, list becomes Vec<serde_json::Value> and tuple/set/frozenset become JSON; PyO3 and pyo3 each appear zero times in sk-code so the Python half has no home

A project type may cross as JSON only after an admission test with five named conditions covering visibility, single declaration, no argument-taking constructor, no public instance fields and at least one crossing property; sk-code permits passive boundary structs but never defines passive

The port signature is Result<T, String> which sk-code's P1 typed-domain-error rule forbids; resolved by scope, the port stub is a scaffold and sk-code governs the shipped boundary, so the edit is to say a scaffold may use a stringly error and a shipped boundary may not

TypeScript number becomes f64 faithful to JS and sk-code's version of the same rule is stricter, requiring explicit finite-value and numeric-parity handling; this row should be left alone and recorded so the edit list does not fix a rule that is already better
